html:
Italian Somaliland was the Italian colony in southern Somalia, built up from protectorates over coastal sultanates from 1889 and ruled with Mogadishu as its capital.

Italy put land along the Juba and Shebelle rivers into banana and cotton plantations worked by forced labour. In 1936 the colony became part of Italian East Africa after the invasion of Ethiopia, and Britain took it in 1941.

From 1950 Italy ran it again for ten years as a United Nations trust territory, with a promise of independence, and it built up a Somali civil service. On 1 July 1960 it united with British Somaliland to form the Somali Republic.
sum: Italian Somaliland was the Italian colony in southern Somalia, built up from protectorates over coastal sultanates from 1889 and ruled with Mogadishu as its capital.
